question:
A 38-year-old woman comes to the outpatient clinic for her routine annual wellness examination. She
has no specific complaints but mentions during the review of systems that she has experienced an
increased frequency of headaches over the past 8 months, which typically resolve with rest or
acetaminophen. Aside from acetaminophen for occasional pain, she only takes a daily vitamin D
supplement. Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago, and her cycles are regular. She does not
smoke and consumes about one alcoholic drink per week. Vital signs are normal, and a comprehensive
physical examination reveals no abnormalities. On structural examination, tenderness is noted in the
paravertebral muscles of the cervical region. Active motion testing indicates restricted rotation of the
head to the right compared to the left, while gross sidebending of the cervical spine is symmetrical.
Starting from a neutral position, what is the initial setup for muscle energy treatment for this patient’s
most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Slightly flex the neck, sidebend the neck left, and rotate the
head left (B) Flex neck 30°, bilateral rotation (C) Neutral position, sidebend right with slight rotation left
(D) Rotate the head to the left (E) Flex the neck 45°, sidebend to the right (F) Extend the neck 30°,
rotate the head to the right (G) Extend the neck fully, rotate to the left (H) Slight extension with right
rotation (I) Flex the neck 30°, sidebend to the left, and rotate to the right (J) Flex the neck 45°, rotate
the head to the right
 A. Slightly flex the neck, sidebend the neck left, and rotate the head left
B. Rotate the head to the left
C. Neutral position, sidebend right with slight rotation left
D. Flex the neck 30°, sidebend to the left, and rotate to the right
E. Extend the neck fully, rotate to the left
F. Extend the neck 30°, rotate the head to the right
G. Flex the neck 45°, sidebend to the right
H. Flex neck 30°, bilateral rotation
I. Flex the neck 45°, rotate the head to the right
J. Slight extension with right rotation
